source: Homer, Odyssey (Greek), khora EOT first 120000 chars; scene cuts by the base driver scene-kinds.mjs (bayes>.90pct + position-vocabulary, MIN_LEN 4) -> 68 scenes; the first 30 hand-labelled.
reader: one reader's judgment, disclosed — NOT ground truth from the text, NOT fed to any inducer.
disclosure: Scene indices are the base driver's mechanical cuts (scene:i == i-th run of clauses). The cuts are pragmatic, not narrative: 3/4 and 28/29 re-read the same sentence, and several scenes (esp. 14, 17) are multi-situation bags. Each scene is labelled with the SINGLE best human action-situation type; ties/mixtures are named in notes. Labels are the judge's, formed by reading the raw Greek, not derived from any induced kind.

types.proem: metapoetic invocation/epitome (Muse, the hero's epitome) — a frame, not an enacted situation.
types.assembly: deliberative gathering: the Olympian council or the Ithacan agora — convocation, speeches, a decision or dissolution.
types.reception: xenia: host welcomes guest — hand-clasp, spear taken, seating, hand-washing.
types.feast: communal meal: food/wine served, suitors carousing, the table as arena.
types.gossip: exchange of news/identity/genealogy in conversation (who are you, whence, tell of the father).
types.omen: prophecy or bird-sign and its interpretation (divination).
types.counsel: advice/instruction: an elder/guest telling the young hero what to do (planning).
types.intrigue: dolos/plot: the loom trick, the suitors' ambush scheme, malicious planning.
types.prayer: supplication/invocation of a god by a mortal (hand-washing + vow).
types.voyage: we-Voyage: travel, ship, crew, the journey undertaken or declared.
types.landing: arrival/epiphany: a god or traveller comes to a place.

notes.0: Muse-invocation + epitome; embeds the Helios-cattle taboo and the destruction of the crew. Frame dominates -> proem.
notes.1: Others home; Odysseus kept by Calypso; the gods gather in Zeus's halls and the father of gods begins speeches -> divine assembly convenes.
notes.2: Zeus's speech (Aegisthus/Orestes) + Athena's reply: a council debate recounting an intrigue/destruction.
notes.3: Athena, in council, on Odysseus suffering on Calypso's sea-navel island.
notes.4: Athena's plea over Odysseus; Calypso beguiles him; his piety to the gods.
notes.5: Council resolution: Hermes to Calypso; Athena to Ithaca to stir Telemachus and call an assembly.
notes.6: Athena arms, descends Olympus, reaches Odysseus's porch disguised as Mentes; finds the suitors at dice -> arrival.
notes.7: Telemachus sees the guest first, goes out, takes his hand and the bronze spear -> reception.
notes.8: Telemachus receives the guest with welcome words and leads her in -> reception.
notes.9: Inside: spear set in the rack, guest seated on a chair with footstool, hand-washing prepared -> reception.
notes.10: Hand-washing, bread/meats set out, wine poured by the herald -> feast service.
notes.11: Suitors enter and sit, reach for the food, Phemius plays; Telemachus whispers to the guest -> feast.
notes.12: Telemachus asks the stranger who he is, how he sailed, who his crew were -> gossip.
notes.13: Mentes's travel account (ship, crew, Temese for bronze, iron) + guest-friendship claim -> gossip.
notes.14: Mentes foretells: Odysseus lives, will return; the stranger resembles him; the feast questioned. Prophecy dominates.
notes.15: Telemachus's answer: the lost father, the suitors devouring the house, the imagined vengeance -> narration/gossip.
notes.16: Mentes instructs: summon the assembly tomorrow, send the suitors off, send Penelope to her father -> counsel.
notes.17: Mentes's detailed voyage/vengeance advice, Telemachus's thanks, Athena's bird-departure (epiphany), Phemius's song, Penelope's weeping and her rebuke -> counsel dominates the bag; disclose the embedded omen/epiphany.
notes.18: Night confrontation in the halls: Telemachus's challenge, Antinous's mockery, Eurymachus on the gods' knees -> suitor feast/agora-in-embryo.
notes.19: Eurymachus asks after the stranger's origin and whether he brings news of the father -> gossip.
notes.20: Telemachus's reply, night and the suitors' departure, then the herald calls the assembly and Aegyptius speaks -> assembly convoked.
notes.21: In the agora: Aegyptius asks who called; Telemachus rises and voices his grief -> assembly.
notes.22: Telemachus's plea; Antinous blames Penelope and recounts the loom trick (dolos), discovered -> intrigue recounted at the assembly.
notes.23: Telemachus refuses to expel his mother (Furies), repeats 'kill me'; the suitors marvel -> assembly.
notes.24: Halitherses reads the eagle-omen and prophesies Odysseus's return and vengeance; Eurymachus mocks -> omen.
notes.25: Eurymachus's retort; Telemachus requests a ship and crew; Mentor rebukes the demos -> assembly.
notes.26: Mentor dissolves the assembly; Telemachus prays to Athena by the sea; Athena (as Mentor) promises a ship -> prayer.
notes.27: Antinous mocks Telemachus; Telemachus declares he will sail (as passenger) -> voyage declared.
notes.28: The suitors speculate: will he bring avengers from Pylos/Sparta, or poison from Ephyra to kill us? -> intrigue.
notes.29: A youth: who knows if he dies at sea; then we divide the estate and marry the mother -> intrigue.
